artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: New LegacyUploader: opens progress.sqlite3 mode=ro, reads article_objects (83) + article_links (84) READ-ONLY, puts each stored normalised-record file's bytes as bronze via harvest_grammar.put_article_bronze(..., received_form="normalised_record") -- the ONE writer (ruling 2, unchanged) -- and rebuilds the silver article row from those SAME bytes via silver_from_bronze.article_rows(), with discovery filled from every link the article carries (discovered_for = every linked security_key, first_discovered_at = the earliest link, retrieval_rung = symbol_listing for sa else name_search, search_query = the linked pilot security's sa_symbol for sa else its company). Rows are grouped by (source, run_stamp) -- their own shared value -- and written with ONE silver_append call per group via _silver_append_retrying_object_name, which retries a PreconditionFailed under a suffixed run_stamp rather than colliding forever on a key a same-second sibling (or an earlier partial run) already occupies; never deletes anything.

New `upload-legacy` command choice, dispatched BEFORE Worker(root, config) is constructed (that constructor opens progress.sqlite3 READ-WRITE) so the CLI path never touches the real database in write mode -- matches LegacyUploader's own mode=ro contract. New `upload-harvest` command makes the already-built HarvestUploader reachable from the CLI for the first time (HVST-h-10 uses it). Both take the existing --runtime-root flag and the new --retrieval-mode flag (choices backfill/live, default live); no path hardcoded.

New file, exactly the six arms section 1 item 4 names, over a temp SQLite FILE (never :memory: -- LegacyUploader opens the file by path) and a STUB S3 client (same shape as lib/research/harvest/tests/test_store.py). No network, no vendor call, no live bucket.

83 bronze objects (one per legacy article_objects row) live in opal-data-harvest, put with metadata received-form=normalised_record. Verified by AC6: head_object succeeded on 83 of 83 keys named in the receipt's bronze_keys, and every one carries received-form=normalised_record (0 overlap with the 6 pre-existing seeking-alpha REST-channel bronze objects, confirmed by hash comparison before the first live run).

83 silver article rows live in opal-data-harvest (one per legacy article), reached across two live runs after the object-name-collision fix: the first post-fix run wrote the remaining 15 not-yet-written rows (errors 0), and the run captured as this cell's literal AC4/AC5 evidence found the corpus fully settled (bronze_put 0, silver_rows_written 0, silver_rows_unchanged 83, errors 0 on both). Four same-second SA groups (19 articles) that previously deadlocked on a stale part-<run_stamp>.parquet key now resolve via the suffix-retry.
The literal AC4 invocation's teed receipt; committed together with this instance at the complete flip.
